implementation_notes: Go's documented pipeline idiom is the whole composite: the splitter feeds a jobs channel, one goroutine per worker drains it, results return on a single channel, and a sync.WaitGroup over the senders closes that channel so the aggregator's range loop terminates exactly when the last part is done - the Go blog calls this fan-out/fan-in. The routing decision is a switch in the dispatcher (or one jobs channel per part kind), and the aggregate is a fold in the collector; the channel carries the part index, so no shared memory is needed.
code_sketch:
jobs := make(chan Part)
results := make(chan Result)
var wg sync.WaitGroup
for i := 0; i < workers; i++ {
    wg.Add(1)
    go func() { defer wg.Done(); for p := range jobs { results <- route(p) } }()
}
go func() { for _, p := range split(msg) { jobs <- p }; close(jobs) }()
go func() { wg.Wait(); close(results) }()
report := Report{}
for r := range results { report.Merge(r) }        // aggregation
pitfalls: Close the results channel only after close(jobs) and wg.Wait(); closing it earlier panics with a send on closed channel.
Returning early from the aggregator leaves workers blocked on the results channel - goroutines are not garbage collected (the Go blog documents this leak); use buffering or a done channel.
An unbounded goroutine per part is not a worker pool: large composites need workers derived from a bound, not len(parts).

variants.name: golang.org/x/sync/errgroup with a bounded limit
variants.implementation_notes: errgroup layers two things over the same fan-out that a composed processor actually needs: the first part error cancels the derived context so the siblings stop, and SetLimit bounds concurrency without a hand-rolled semaphore. Results go into a preallocated slice indexed by part position, so the correlation state is still an index rather than a map. Prefer it when one failed part must abort the composite; keep the bare channel fan-in when a partial aggregate must survive individual part failures.
variants.code_sketch:
g, ctx := errgroup.WithContext(ctx)
g.SetLimit(8)
results := make([]Result, len(parts))
for i, p := range parts {
    i, p := i, p
    g.Go(func() error { r, err := route(ctx, p); results[i] = r; return err })
}
if err := g.Wait(); err != nil { return Report{}, err }   // fail the composite
return merge(results), nil
pitfalls: Writing results[i] is race-free only because each goroutine owns one index; a shared accumulator still needs a mutex.
SetLimit's Go blocks once the limit is reached, so calling Go from inside a limited goroutine that holds the last slot self-deadlocks.
A failed part cancels the context: parts that do not observe ctx keep working, so the aggregate must not assume all sibling work stopped.
